fields.statement: Verified at 20947c77. go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow/... ok. go test -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/run-ship-(landed-)?infra-wait' PASS for run-ship-infra-wait and run-ship-landed-infra-wait. rhiza workflow check ship-change is valid (builtin). workflow describe shows rebase-merge-gate-failed on.fail -> landed-infra-triage (rhiza ship check --infra) -> landed-infra-wait -> landed-green; the built-in wait runs until 'rhiza ship check --settled --changed --rerun-infra' with timeout 6h, interval 30s and max_visits 3; gate-fix-merge stays on.pass. Read the diff of run-ship-landed-infra-wait.txtar. The fake gh's check is Actions run 42 with logs naming no failing test. wait-landed spends one rerun and the head is still red. landed-green, conflict-triage-landed and rebase-merge-gate-failed then fail through to landed-infra-triage and landed-infra-wait. The wait's own 'gh run rerun 42 --failed' comes right after a --rerun-infra poll, and the script never reruns. A bin/rhiza shim moves red_at back so that rerun is due. The head turns green, and the run goes on through gate-rebase-merge, rebase-merge, a squash merge pinned to the green head, wait-main, main-green and close-out (asserted in run status and gh.log). This fixes both earlier findings: merge and close-out are now reached, and the rerun now comes from the wait.
